name: Senjuohashi
tagline: Otemachi in 25 minutes and Tokyo in 26 minutes. Served by 1 line. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥80,000 to ¥90,000.
summary: The station is in Adachi City, served by Keisei Main Line. Journey times to the main business districts are 25 minutes to Otemachi, 37 minutes to Shinjuku, 45 minutes to Shibuya and 40 minutes to Shinagawa. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥80,000 to ¥90,000. The station stands 0.7 m above sea level, and the ground within 800 m varies in height by 3.0 m. The land around the station is close to level.

terrain.note: The station sits lower than the ground around it, at 0.7 m above sea level. Within 800 m the ground ranges from 0.2 m to 3.2 m, a difference of 3.0 m.

hazards: On the flood hazard map for the largest rainfall the government models, the station itself falls inside the projected inundation area, to a projected depth of 5 to 10 m. All nine points within 400 m of the station fall inside the area too, and the deepest projection among them is 5 to 10 m. On the whole, the flood projection here is on the large side for the 23 wards.
medical: Within an 800 m walk of the station there are 6 clinics and 6 pharmacies. Day-to-day care is available close to the station. The nearest hospital is 愛里病院, about 13 minutes' walk from the station. The next nearest is 勝楽堂病院, about 20 minutes' walk. "Hospital" here means a facility OpenStreetMap records as one. OpenStreetMap does not record whether a facility admits inpatients or which departments it runs, so check each one on its own website. For which clinics open at night and at weekends, ask the emergency advice line of the ward you live in.
stationNote: 1 line serve the station: Keisei Main Line.
congestion: Keisei Main Line runs at 137% of capacity in the morning peak. The busiest stretch is 大神宮下→京成船橋, which this station is not on. At 100%, the ministry's scale describes every passenger either seated or able to hold a strap or pillar. The figures describe each line's busiest stretch, so the stretch you ride may be easier.

rentRange.note: Around this station, One room ¥80,000 to ¥90,000 and 1K ¥90,000 to ¥100,000. 1LDK ¥160,000 to ¥170,000 and 2LDK ¥200,000 to ¥210,000. These are the per-station averages published by LIFULL HOME'S, Yahoo! Real Estate and at home, averaged together and rounded down to the nearest ¥10,000 (our own survey). All three are asking rents, so what tenants finally agree can be lower. Within the same station area the figure moves a great deal with the age of the building, the walk from the station, and whether the flat faces a main road.

rentReason: A one-room flat here goes for ¥80,000 to ¥90,000. Set against how long it takes to reach the central business districts, that is about average for the 23 wards. In plain yen, though, it is on the low side for the 23 wards. For 1LDK, 2LDK, though, the sources differ by ¥30,000 or more. They count different sets of properties, so read those figures as a range rather than a point.

neighbours.lead: For rail connections, Minami-Senju; for lower rent, Senjuohashi.
neighbours.note: About 1 km from Senjuohashi in a straight line. Minami-Senju also has the JR Joban Line, Tokyo Metro Hibiya Line and Tsukuba Express, which Senjuohashi does not. With more lines, Minami-Senju is the better connected of the two. To Toranomon, for instance, Minami-Senju is 9 minutes quicker. A one-room flat, though, costs about ¥14,000 more at Minami-Senju.

neighbours.lead: For rail connections, Kita-Senju; for safety, Senjuohashi.
neighbours.note: About 1 km from Senjuohashi in a straight line. Kita-Senju has 5 lines that Senjuohashi does not. With more lines, Kita-Senju is the better connected of the two. To Toranomon, for instance, Kita-Senju is 7 minutes quicker. On what it offers families, though, Senjuohashi comes out ahead.

noiseSources: 日光街道 (2 lanes each way) runs right beside the station, so for a flat close to the station, check whether it faces the road
The nearest big road, 墨堤通り, is far enough that little traffic noise reaches the station area

leads.terrain: The ground around the station is almost level, so you can choose where to live without thinking about slopes.
leads.groceries: There are 4 supermarkets within walking distance, and the nearest is 3 minutes on foot.
leads.hazards: The station itself sits inside the area projected to flood in the heaviest rainfall the government models.
leads.stationNote: Only the Keisei Main Line serves this station, so when it stops you walk to another station.
leads.rentRange: The balance between commuting time and rent is about average for the 23 wards.
leads.medical: The number of clinics and pharmacies within walking distance is about average for the 23 wards.
leads.congestion: Among the 23 wards' stations, the lines here are lightly loaded in the morning.
